A smart person who was given a chunk of someone else's land would rent it back to them, if that was allowed. A smart government would not take it from them in the first place! I sympathise with the idea that land does not belong to the people who are using it (because they didn't create it), but basic economics tells us we should let the best qualified people use it and let them employ as much capital on the land as they see fit, not distribute it between thousands of peasant workers. A smart government interested in land reform would levy a tax on the value of the land instead of stealing it.

Econ 101: Large farms where capital replaces labor produce more food at lower cost and free up labor to work in factories, service industries etc. This results in more production, which raises living standards for all people including the poor. Small farms run by unskilled workers with no machinery produce less food and must feed the owners before any surplus can be sold (they are much closer to subsistence level than the agri-business is). The amount of food and labor available to non-agricultural industries is severely reduced, lower output leads to hunger and poverty.
